{{< include /knowledge/includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}
This isn't a theoretical plan. It's a greatest hits album of things that already worked.

Before you say "this is impossible," let me remind you: humans have accidentally done smart things before. Not often. But occasionally, when properly motivated by fear or greed (usually both), your species stumbles into competence.

You've done every single part of this plan already. You just haven't combined them yet. You're like someone who owns flour, water, yeast, and an oven, but keeps eating them separately and wondering why bread hasn't appeared.

## The Immune System

Your brain is about to generate objections. This is normal. Every brain does it. The objections feel original but they are not. There are fifteen of them. We have heard all of them, on every planet, in approximately the same order. Each one corresponds to a specific stage of resistance, and each one has a specific door through it.

Here is the complete map. Every wall your brain will build, and the chapter that demolishes it.

### Stage 1: "Why should I care?"

Your brain says: *this doesn't affect me. Things are fine. Death is natural.*

| What you'll think | Why it's wrong | Where it's addressed |
|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| "I won't suffer that badly" | You cannot disprove eternal suffering. Time dilation is documented. P > 0 is enough when the stakes are infinite. | [Wishonia's Wager](proof/wishonias-wager.qmd) |
| "Living forever is impossible" | At least one species is already biologically immortal. No law of physics prevents it. | [The Body as a Repairable Machine](proof/body-as-repairable-machine.qmd) |
| "Death is natural and inevitable" | 92% of death is from disease. Disease is treatable. "Natural" is not "inevitable." | [The Cost of Disease](problem/cost-of-disease.qmd) |
| "I'm too small to matter" | You are the entire universe from your own perspective. "I'm too small" is the delusion, not grandeur. The solipsist and the altruist arrive at the same action. | [The Delusion of Insignificance](proof/delusion-of-insignificance.qmd) |

### Stage 2: "Is this real?"

Your brain says: *this sounds crazy. Someone would have fixed this. I'd need to do more research.*

| What you'll think | Why it's wrong | Where it's addressed |
|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| "I might lose money" | One option is better in every scenario. There is no scenario where doing nothing wins. | [Where Am I Wrong?](appendix/where-am-i-wrong.qmd) |
| "I don't believe in this cause" | You already spend money on food, shelter, and medicine. Your spending proves you prefer survival. NOT acting on that preference is the inconsistency. | [Frequently Asked Objections](appendix/faq.qmd) |
| "Someone smarter would have fixed this" | The system selects against whoever would fix it. The skills that get you INTO power are orthogonal to the skills needed to OPTIMIZE the system. | [Why Hasn't Anyone Done This?](proof/why-hasnt-anyone-done-this.qmd) |

### Stage 3: "How does it work?"

Your brain says: *okay, but what can I actually do? One person can't change this.*

| What you'll think | Why it's wrong | Where it's addressed |
|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| "I can't afford to help" | $200 buys one share. One share gives you legal standing. Legal standing lets you file a letter the board must respond to. | [The Loving Takeover](appendix/loving-takeover.qmd) |
| "The companies will fight back" | Fighting back proves the thesis. Every response feeds the loop. The lobbying destroys its own funding source. | [Frequently Asked Objections](appendix/faq.qmd) |
| "One person can't change anything" | One can't. A thousand can. The loop compounds. Each new person increases the value for everyone. | [Frequently Asked Objections](appendix/faq.qmd) |
| "Your analysis might be wrong" | Any analysis beats zero analysis. The current baseline is zero. Being better than nothing is not a high bar. | [Where Am I Wrong?](appendix/where-am-i-wrong.qmd) |

### Stage 4: "Why me? Why now?"

Your brain says: *I'll think about it. I have other priorities. Maybe later.*

| What you'll think | Why it's wrong | Where it's addressed |
|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| "I have better uses for my money" | Your money is worthless the moment you die. Every dollar loses value every day because you're closer to death. The $200 preserves the value of everything else you own. | [Your Personal Benefits](call-to-action/your-personal-benefits.qmd) |
| "I'll do it later" | This mechanism is discoverable from public data. Someone will do it with or without you. Delay means someone else defines the terms. | [Frequently Asked Objections](appendix/faq.qmd) |

### Stage 5: "What's the endgame?"

Your brain says: *even if this works, people won't change. The system is too broken.*

| What you'll think | Why it's wrong | Where it's addressed |
|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| "People will never change" | Laziness, stupidity, and greed are biochemical states. All three are partially curable now. The cure is underfunded 604:1. | [Every Human Defect is Curable](problem/i-am-retarded.qmd) |
| "The system can't be fixed" | Your leader is a neural network with documented defects. A testable, transparent system produces better outputs. The processor is replaceable. | [Optimocracy: The Evidence Machine](solution/optimocracy.qmd) |

Fifteen walls. Fifteen doors. Organized by the order your brain will build them. If you find a wall without a door, email wishonia@gmail.com and we will write a new proof. Until then, this is the complete set.

## Three Proofs That Close Every Exit {#three-proofs}

The case for redirecting resources (from things that kill people to things that stop people dying) rests on three independent proofs. Each one is sufficient alone. Together, they leave no rational exit.

1. **The Rational Proof.** [Wishonia's Wager](proof/wishonias-wager.qmd) establishes that when outcomes include any nonzero probability of indefinite suffering or indefinite flourishing, any finite action that shifts the odds is rational. The expected value of inaction is infinitely bad. The cost of action is finite. The math does not require you to believe anything specific. It requires you to accept that you cannot prove the probability is zero.

2. **The Obligatory Proof.** [The Biotechnological Imperative](proof/biotechnological-imperative.qmd) applies Kant's categorical imperative: can you universalize "spend resources on killing instead of curing"? No. A civilization that does this goes extinct. Therefore redirecting resources from weapons to medicine is not optional. It is a categorical duty. The math from Wishonia's Wager says you *should* act. Kant says you *must*.

3. **The Proven Proof.** The [free market mechanism](solution/wishocracy.qmd) has been tested for centuries. [Wishocracy](solution/wishocracy.qmd) [@wishocracy-paper-2025] applies it to public spending. The objection "this is untested" is false. The objection "this is unprecedented" is false. The only thing that is new is applying a proven mechanism to a domain your species inexplicably exempted from it.

Rational. Obligatory. Proven. Pick any one. The conclusion is the same.

Now, the historical evidence that every component of this plan has already worked somewhere, on this planet, performed by your own species, usually by accident.

## Pragmatic Trials: {{< var dfda_trial_cost_reduction_factor >}} More Efficient {#pragmatic-trials}

Traditional Phase 3 trials cost {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}} [@trial-costs-fda-study].
Pragmatic trials embedded in routine care cost {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} [@pragmatic-trials-cost-advantage], a **{{< var dfda_trial_cost_reduction_factor >}} cost reduction**.

![The British figured out how to test drugs for $929 per patient. Americans spend $41,000. Both countries speak English, so language barrier isn't the issue.](/assets/images/proof/proof-section-pragmatic-trials-44-1x-95-ci-39-4x-89-1x-more-efficient-bw-academic.jpg)

A Harvard meta-analysis of 108 embedded pragmatic trials found median costs of just $97 per patient [@embedded-pragmatic-trials-meta-analysis]. The ALLHAT trial showed pragmatic designs can identify superior treatments and reduced healthcare costs by billions annually [@ford2016]. So the cheap way is also the better way. Happens more often than you'd think.

Oxford's RECOVERY trial achieved {{< var recovery_trial_cost_per_patient >}}. It found life-saving COVID treatments in under 100 days. It saved over a million lives [@recovery-trial-1m-lives-saved].

## Humans Doing Smart Things (Accidentally): A Collection {#historical-precedents}

### That Time Humans Banned Landmines (Yes, Really) {#landmine-treaty}

**What happened:** A bunch of NGOs decided landmines were bad actually. They convinced 160 nations to sign a treaty banning them [@icbl-ottawa-treaty] in 1997. Major military powers initially opposed it. The NGOs won anyway.

![Some activists with clipboards convinced 160 countries to ban landmines while America, Russia, and China said no. The landmines are still banned. Democracy works in mysterious ways.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-that-time-humans-banned-landmines-yes-really-bw-academic.jpg)

**Why this matters for you:** This proves citizen movements can create binding international law even when governments don't want to. If humans can globally ban a weapon because "it's mean," you can definitely redirect 1% of the murder budget to the not-murder budget. And they did it with fax machines. Just pissed-off citizens with fax machines. You have the internet.

### War Bonds: That Time Grandma Funded WW2 {#war-bonds}

**What happened:** Governments needed money to fight Nazis. They sold "war bonds" (basically IOUs that paid interest) directly to regular people. Promise them profit + dead Nazis. Kill Nazis, earn 2.9%. Good deal. The U.S. raised $185 billion [@wwii-war-bonds] (trillions in today's dollars [@wwii-cost-4-trillion-today]).

**Why this matters for you:** Your grandparents gave the government money to stop Hitler and got 2.9% returns. You're offering {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns to stop cancer. [VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025] are the same thing except with better ROI and fewer Nazis (hopefully zero Nazis). Except instead of dead Nazis, you offer dead cancer cells.

The formula worked: mix moral incentives (patriotism) with financial self-interest (interest payments). You're applying it to a different war: the one against your own mortality. When saving the world is profitable, people trip over each other to fund it.

![War Bonds: give us money, we'll build bombs, you might get paid back. VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds: give us money, we'll cure diseases, you definitely get paid back. One of these sells better.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-incentive-alignment-bonds-comparison-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Global Fund (Proof That New Health Institutions Can Exist) {#global-fund}

**What happened:** In 2002, the world created a new organization [@global-fund] to pool billions for fighting AIDS, TB, and malaria. It bypassed traditional bureaucracies and just... worked. Saved an estimated 65 million lives [@global-fund-50-million-lives-saved] (as of 2024). Bureaucrats everywhere were horrified.

![Started fighting AIDS, TB, and malaria. Realized other diseases also exist. Expanded accordingly. This took decades.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-the-global-fund-proof-that-new-health-institutions-can-exist-bw-academic.jpg)

**Why this matters for you:** A network of [Decentralized Institutes of Health](solution/dih.qmd) ([DIH](solution/dih.qmd)) isn't fantasy. It's the Global Fund but bigger and for all diseases. If you can create new health institutions for three diseases, you can create one for all of them. It's multiplication. You learned this when you were six.

### Post-WW2: That Time America Accidentally Discovered Peace Is Profitable {#post-ww2}

**What happened:** 1945: US military spending was 37% of GDP [@us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut] (we were very serious about the war thing). 1948: Cut to 7%. That's a 30 percentage point drop. Not 1%. THIRTY.

**The results:** The greatest economic boom in human history:

  - GDP growth: 8% yearly for a decade [@us-post-wwii-gdp-growth-8-pct] (vs normal 2-3%)
  - Home ownership doubled [@us-post-wwii-home-ownership-doubled] (middle class explosion)
  - GI Bill created modern knowledge economy
  - Built the interstate highway system

**Why this matters for you:** You're redirecting 1%. America cut {{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}} in constant dollars (from {{< var us_military_spending_1945_peak_annual_2024usd >}} to {{< var us_military_spending_1947_annual_2024usd >}} in today's money) and got rich [@us-military-spending-historical-constant-dollars]. Today you spend {{< var us_military_spending_current_vs_prewar_multiplier >}} the pre-WW2 baseline. You proved you could cut {{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}} and thrive. Now you spend {{< var us_military_spending_current_vs_prewar_multiplier >}} the pre-war baseline and someone is asking for 1% back. I showed these numbers to a Wishonian economist and she assumed they were a typo. I showed them to a second economist and she assumed the first one was right. I showed them to a third and she asked if Earth was currently fighting 30 simultaneous world wars. I said no, just the one on terror, and it was making things worse. She asked me to stop talking about Earth because it was upsetting her.

![After World War II, America cut military spending by 90 percent and became the richest country on Earth. We learned absolutely nothing from this.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-post-ww2-economic-impact-bw-academic.jpg)

### The 1990s: When the Berlin Wall Fell and Wallets Exploded {#cold-war-dividend}

**What happened:** Cold War ended. Military spending dropped from 6% of GDP to 3%. That's roughly $50 billion a year redirected from pointing missiles at Russia to literally anything else.

![When the Cold War ended, we stopped building so many missiles and accidentally invented the internet. Imagine what we could invent on purpose.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-the-1990s-when-the-berlin-wall-fell-and-wallets-exploded-bw-academic.jpg)

**The results:** The 1990s economic boom everyone remembers fondly:

  - Internet became commercial (freed resources)
  - First budget surplus in 30 years
  - Unemployment: 3.9% (lowest in a generation)
  - Productivity: +2.5% yearly (double the normal rate)

**Why this matters for you:** The pattern isn't subtle. Every time you stop spending money on murder, prosperity appears like magic. It's not magic. It's arithmetic. You just keep forgetting the answer.

### Switzerland: 200 Years of Not Shooting Anyone = Being Very Rich {#switzerland}

Two world wars. Everyone else fought. Switzerland made chocolate.

**What they have:** Mountains, cows, and a complete lack of natural resources. They're surrounded by countries that kept starting world wars. They have been neutral since 1815.

![Switzerland spends less on military than its neighbors and is much richer. They also make excellent chocolate. These facts may be related.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-switzerland-200-years-of-not-shooting-anyone-being-very-rich-bw-academic.jpg)

**What they spend on defense:** {{< var switzerland_defense_spending_pct >}} of GDP (source [@swiss-military-budget-0-7-pct-gdp]) (purely defensive; they're not invading anyone with those Alps) (US: {{< var us_military_spending_pct_gdp >}})

#### The results

  - {{< var switzerland_gdp_per_capita_k >}} GDP per capita [@swiss-vs-us-gdp-per-capita] (vs US $76K), 25% richer than Americans
  - Universal healthcare, excellent quality, 12% of GDP (vs US 18%)
  - Life expectancy: 84 years [@swiss-vs-us-life-expectancy] (vs US 79)
  - Last invaded: 1798 (Napoleon succeeded, briefly; the Swiss waited him out, then went back to being Switzerland)
  - Haven't had a war death since 1847 [@switzerland-last-war-death-1847]

The difference went to education, healthcare, and trains that run on time. (Americans: a "train that runs on time" is a train that arrives when it says it will. I know this sounds fictional.)

**Why this matters for you:** Peace dividends compound over centuries. Switzerland proves you don't need oil, colonies, or weapons to get rich. Just stop wasting money on things that explode. They've been doing this for 200 years. You're asking for a 1% start.

![Switzerland spends less on weapons and lives longer. America spends more on weapons and dies sooner. Science is still investigating whether these facts are related.](/assets/images/proof/proof-section-switzerland-peace-dividend-bw-academic.jpg)

## When Good Intentions Met Reality (And Lost) {#cautionary-tales}

Failures teach more than successes. Here's every mistake past movements made, so you can make exciting new ones instead.

### Eisenhower's Warning: A 5-Star General Tried to Tell You {#eisenhower}

In 1961, President Dwight D. Eisenhower used his farewell address to warn you about something terrifying. He was a 5-star general. Supreme Allied Commander. The guy who beat the Nazis. Not exactly a hippie.

**The warning:** "We must guard against the military-industrial complex."

![Every bomber built is a hospital not built, said the five-star general. Then everyone ignored him and built more bombers. He knew how these things go.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-eisenhower-s-warning-a-5-star-general-tried-to-tell-you-bw-academic.jpg)

**The reality check:** "Every gun made, every warship launched, every rocket fired signifies theft from those who hunger."

**The prophecy:** He predicted the permanent war economy you're currently living in. Military spending becomes self-perpetuating regardless of whether anyone's actually threatening you.

**Why this matters:** Eisenhower understood you can't dismantle the system. You have to give it something more profitable to build. He was right. Nobody listened. You never do. Now you get to try his solution: redirect the resources.

### The Nuclear Freeze Movement: Millions of People, Zero Results {#nuclear-freeze}

**What happened:** In the 1980s, a massive global movement [@nuclear-disarmament-movement-freeze] tried to freeze nuclear weapons production. Millions of protesters. Enormous popular support. Good vibes everywhere.

![Asking explosion manufacturers to be nice doesn't work. Offering them biotech profits does. Greed is easier to redirect than eliminate.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-the-nuclear-freeze-movement-millions-of-people-zero-results-bw-academic.jpg)

**The result:** Failed completely. Nuclear arsenals kept growing. The signs were very moving, though.

**Why it failed:** You cannot defeat money with good intentions. The military-industrial complex has more money than God, and protesters have signs. This is why a [1% Treaty](solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-percent-treaty-paper-2025] [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] doesn't ask nicely; it bribes everyone into compliance. You're not fighting greed. You're redirecting it. Morality is lovely. Capitalism is faster.

**The lesson:** Make peace more profitable than war, or peace loses. Every single time. No exceptions. I checked.

### Occupy Wall Street: When "We're Angry" Isn't a Strategy {#occupy}

**What happened:** In 2011, thousands occupied parks [@occupy-wall-street] to protest economic inequality.
They changed the conversation!
They raised awareness!
They accomplished nothing permanent!

![Occupy Wall Street had 50 demands and changed nothing. We have one demand. This is either much smarter or much sadder.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-occupy-wall-street-when-we-re-angry-isn-t-a-strategy-bw-academic.jpg)

**Why it failed:** No specific demand.
Just diffuse anger at "the system."
The energy dissipated because nobody knew what success looked like.

**Why this matters:** This plan has ONE demand: ratify a [1% Treaty](solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd).
That's it.
Not "fix inequality" or "be better."
One specific, achievable, measurable goal.
You want to change one number from 0 to 1.
Ambition is inspiring, but subtraction is effective.
A network of [Decentralized Institutes of Health](solution/dih.qmd) (DIH), a [decentralized FDA](solution/dfda.qmd) [@dfda-spec-paper-2025; @dfda-impact-paper-2025], and the cures are all downstream of that single objective.

When you ask for everything, you get nothing.
When you ask for 1%, you might get it.

## On How Rich People Made Money Doing Crazy Things (And Why That Matters) {#financial-precedents}

You need investment terms that don't sound insane to people with money. Fortunately, rich people have always done insane things with money. You just need to make this the least insane option.

### On The Time Junk Bonds Saved Capitalism {#milken}

#### Michael Milken & High-Yield ("Junk") Bonds

In the 1980s, a guy named Michael Milken figured out something revolutionary: if you offer people high enough returns, they'll invest in almost anything [@milken-high-yield-bonds].

![Safe bonds pay 3 percent. Risky bonds pay 8 percent. World peace bonds pay 12 percent. Turns out you can put a price on everything, including virtue.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-michael-milken-high-yield-junk-bonds-bw-academic.jpg)

Wall Street called these "junk bonds" because they were trash. Milken called them "high-yield bonds" because marketing. He financed leveraged buyouts that the establishment said were impossible. He raised billions.

The establishment said it would never work. It worked spectacularly until it didn't (Milken went to prison for unrelated fraud, which is how you know it was successful).

**The Lesson:** To attract capital for high-risk ventures, you must offer absurdly high returns. VICTORY [Incentive Alignment Bonds](https://iab.warondisease.org) promise {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns. This isn't generosity, it's economics. It's the "high-yield" premium necessary to compensate for betting on the unprecedented act of governments doing something smart.

If people invested in literal junk, they'll invest in not dying. You just need to price it correctly.

### On The Time George Soros Broke England {#soros}

#### George Soros & The Quantum Fund

In 1992, George Soros risked $10 billion betting that the UK would have to leave the European Exchange Rate Mechanism [@soros-bet-against-the-pound].

![A diagram illustrating the binary outcomes of Soros's high-stakes bet against the British Pound, showing the tension between private capital and government policy decisions.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-george-soros-the-quantum-fund-bw-academic.jpg)

This was a binary political bet: Either the UK government capitulates, or Soros loses everything.

He won. Made over $1 billion in a single day. The Bank of England lost. The Queen was reportedly not amused. (She had her own money problems, being the Queen.)

**The Lesson:** You can deploy immense private capital to bet on political outcomes. The trick is framing it as sophisticated arbitrage. What it really is: gambling on whether governments will do the obvious thing or the stupid thing.

History suggests governments usually do the stupid thing. But occasionally, when you make the smart thing profitable enough, they surprise you. That's the bet.

### On When Smart People Lost All Their Money (The Cautionary Tales) {#cautionary-finance}

**Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM): When Nobel Laureates Get Humbled**

In 1998, a hedge fund run by actual Nobel Prize winners collapsed. It required a $3.6 billion bailout [@long-term-capital-management-collapse].

![Past financial disasters: no safeguards, pure chaos, everyone loses. This plan: many safeguards, organized chaos, probably fine. Progress is incremental.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-on-when-smart-people-lost-all-their-money-the-cautionary-tales-bw-academic.jpg)

Their crime? Building sophisticated mathematical models that accounted for everything except the part where Russia just... defaults. Whoops.

These were the smartest people in finance. Nobels. PhDs from MIT. Models that predicted everything except reality, which is the one thing models need to predict.

**The Lesson:** Never underestimate systemic risk, also known as "the part where everything goes wrong at once."

For this project, the "black swan" is complete political failure. Everyone says no, the treaty dies, and you look stupid.

This is why the plan includes:

- **Assurance contracts**: Miss the fundraising target? Everyone gets their money back. No partial failures allowed.
- **First-loss philanthropic capital**: Rich altruists absorb the initial losses so regular investors don't get wiped out if things go sideways.

It's risk mitigation for people who understand that Nobel laureates can still be catastrophically wrong.

**The South Sea Bubble (1720): When Everyone Went Insane**

In 1720, people in England went collectively mad. They invested in a company that promised a monopoly on trade with South America [@south-sea-bubble-1720].

Neat! Except the company had almost no actual trade. And no profits. And no business plan beyond "tell people we're going to be really rich."

The stock went up 1,000%. Then it crashed. Everyone lost everything. Isaac Newton lost £20,000 (in today's money, "a lot"). He famously said "I can calculate the motion of heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people."

**The Lesson:** Speculation based on hype alone ends badly.

This is why VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bond payouts are contractually tied to real, verifiable events:

- Treaty ratification (actual government signatures)
- Real government money flowing into the [1% Treaty](solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) Fund
- Actual treatments being tested in pragmatic clinical trials

No hype. No maybes. No "we're going to be really rich someday." Just math tied to observable reality.

If you're going to lose your money, at least it won't be because the plan promised a monopoly on South American trade without checking if South America exists.

## The Ultimate Failsafe: The Worst-Case Scenario is Still a Win {#failsafe}

![Worst case: we reduce global weaponry slightly and waste some money on science. Current case: mountains of bombs and no cancer cure. Hard choice.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-4-the-ultimate-failsafe-the-worst-case-scenario-is-still-a-win-bw-academic.jpg)

Imagine every dollar of the {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} is mismanaged, wasted, or dumped into the ocean.
The world would *still* be better off, because you'd still have a **1% reduction in the global capacity for organized violence**.
Fewer bombs, fewer missiles, fewer AI-powered weapons systems.

![If this fails, we have fewer bombs. If it succeeds, we cure death. These are not symmetrical risks, but we treat them like they are.](/assets/images/historical-precedents/historical-precedents-section-why-bw-academic.jpg)

The worst outcome is still a net gain. The best outcome cures your cancer and your grandmother's Alzheimer's. Failure is still a victory. Success changes the course of human history. It's a bet you can't afford not to take.

## How Your [decentralized FDA](solution/dfda.qmd) Would Compare to History's Best Health Interventions {#dfda-comparison}

The best health investments in history made obscene amounts of money. Smallpox eradication returned hundreds of dollars for every dollar spent. Childhood vaccines, clean water, and tobacco control did similar things. A [decentralized FDA](solution/dfda.qmd) projects even higher returns than any of them: {{< var treaty_roi_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag >}} to 1^[Total societal benefit including lives saved and DALYs averted, not R&D savings alone. R&D-only ROI: {{< var dfda_roi_rd_only >}}:1.].

| Intervention | ROI (per $1) | Cost per QALY | QALYs per $1M |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Decentralized drug assessment** | {{< var treaty_roi_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag >}}:1 | Dominant (cost-saving) | 5,000-90,000+ |
| Smallpox Eradication | 159:1 to 400:1 [@smallpox-eradication-roi] | Dominant | 10,000+ |
| Childhood Vaccination (US) | 10:1 to 16:1 [@childhood-vaccination-roi] | Dominant | 1,000-10,000 |
| Clean Water & Sanitation | 4:1 to 21:1 [@clean-water-sanitation-roi] | Dominant | 1,000-10,000 |
| Tobacco Control | 20:1 to 1,057:1 [@tobacco-control-roi] | Dominant | 1,000-10,000 |

That includes smallpox eradication, which is widely considered the best thing humanity ever did on purpose. The difference: this accelerates the entire research pipeline rather than targeting one disease. It's the difference between fixing one pothole and repaving the road.
